note: Week-ahead plan of simulation ideas for TikTok @studycrest, in making order. Planned by Max and Claude on 14 Nov 2026. Each 'point' is the angle only: every figure and fact must be worked out and verified when the video is made (generator/README.md, Simulation videos, step 2); if the point does not survive checking, tell the true version or skip the idea.

ideas.title: What if the Sun vanished right now?
ideas.setting: A city park at midday
ideas.hook: What if the Sun vanished right now?
ideas.the surprising true point: Nothing changes for about 8 minutes: its light and its gravity both take that long to reach us

ideas.title: Titanic, minute by minute
ideas.setting: The deck and a cutaway of the hull, North Atlantic, 1912
ideas.hook: Titanic, minute by minute
ideas.the surprising true point: The iceberg did not rip one huge hole; narrow openings along the hull flooded too many compartments to stay afloat

ideas.title: What if the Earth stopped spinning for one second?
ideas.setting: A busy city street near the equator
ideas.hook: What if the Earth stopped spinning for one second?
ideas.the surprising true point: The ground stops but you do not: everything loose keeps moving east at the speed the surface was turning

ideas.title: What if you stepped into space without a suit?
ideas.setting: Outside a space station
ideas.hook: What if you stepped into space without a suit?
ideas.the surprising true point: You do not explode or freeze solid; you have seconds of consciousness, and the real danger is the air leaving your lungs and blood

ideas.title: Hindenburg, second by second
ideas.setting: The airship coming in to land, New Jersey, 1937
ideas.hook: Hindenburg, second by second
ideas.the surprising true point: The whole airship burned in well under a minute, and most people on board survived

ideas.title: What if you fell through a tunnel to the other side of the Earth?
ideas.setting: A shaft through the planet, with the Earth cutaway
ideas.hook: What if you fell through a tunnel to the other side of the Earth?
ideas.the surprising true point: You are weightless the whole way, fastest at the centre, and you arrive in about 40 minutes

ideas.title: What if you could see radiation?
ideas.setting: An ordinary kitchen and street
ideas.hook: What if you could see radiation?
ideas.the surprising true point: Everything glows a little: bananas, granite benchtops, and your own body

ideas.title: Apollo 13, second by second
ideas.setting: The spacecraft, 300,000 km from Earth, 1970
ideas.hook: Apollo 13, second by second
ideas.the surprising true point: One oxygen tank failed, and the crew survived by using the lunar lander as a lifeboat

ideas.title: What if a teaspoon of neutron star appeared on your desk?
ideas.setting: A student's desk, then the town
ideas.hook: What if a teaspoon of neutron star appeared on your desk?
ideas.the surprising true point: It would not sit there: without the star's gravity squeezing it, it would blow apart

ideas.title: What if the Moon disappeared tonight?
ideas.setting: A fishing harbour at night
ideas.hook: What if the Moon disappeared tonight?
ideas.the surprising true point: Tides do not stop, they shrink, because the Sun raises tides too

ideas.title: Krakatoa, hour by hour
ideas.setting: The island and the Sunda Strait, 1883
ideas.hook: Krakatoa, hour by hour
ideas.the surprising true point: The loudest sound in recorded history: its pressure wave went around the planet more than once

ideas.title: What if you removed all the empty space from your atoms?
ideas.setting: Inside a hand, zooming down to atoms
ideas.hook: What if you removed all the empty space from your atoms?
ideas.the surprising true point: You would be smaller than a speck of dust and weigh exactly the same; you never truly touch anything

ideas.title: What if you dropped a coin from the top of a skyscraper?
ideas.setting: The city skyline and the street below
ideas.hook: What if you dropped a coin from the top of a skyscraper?
ideas.the surprising true point: Air resistance caps its speed; it stings but it is not a bullet

ideas.title: The first nuclear chain reaction, minute by minute
ideas.setting: Chicago Pile-1 under the stadium stands, 1942
ideas.hook: The first nuclear chain reaction, minute by minute
ideas.the surprising true point: A pile of graphite and uranium, controlled by pulling one rod out by hand

ideas.title: What if all the oxygen vanished for 5 seconds?
ideas.setting: A city street and a beach
ideas.hook: What if all the oxygen vanished for 5 seconds?
ideas.the surprising true point: The viral version is mostly wrong; what really changes is pressure, fire and engines, not buildings turning to dust

ideas.title: What if all the ice on Earth melted?
ideas.setting: A coastal city, sped up over centuries
ideas.hook: What if all the ice on Earth melted?
ideas.the surprising true point: Sea level rises tens of metres, slowly, and the map of every coast is redrawn

ideas.title: Tunguska, second by second
ideas.setting: Siberian forest, 1908
ideas.hook: Tunguska, second by second
ideas.the surprising true point: There is no crater: the object exploded in the air and flattened a forest the size of a city

ideas.title: What if the Earth were crushed into a black hole?
ideas.setting: Earth from space, then a hand holding a marble
ideas.hook: What if the Earth were crushed into a black hole?
ideas.the surprising true point: It would be about the size of a marble, and the Moon would keep orbiting as if nothing happened

ideas.title: What if the lift cable snapped?
ideas.setting: A lift shaft in a skyscraper
ideas.hook: What if the lift cable snapped?
ideas.the surprising true point: Lifts have several cables and automatic brakes on the rails; the film version almost never happens

ideas.title: Pompeii, hour by hour
ideas.setting: The town under Vesuvius, AD 79
ideas.hook: Pompeii, hour by hour
ideas.the surprising true point: It was not lava: fast, hot clouds of gas and ash did the damage, many hours after the eruption began

ideas.title: What if you sank to the deepest point in the ocean?
ideas.setting: The open Pacific, then down past the light to the sea floor
ideas.hook: What if you sank to the deepest point in the ocean?
ideas.the surprising true point: The pressure is around a thousand atmospheres, but you would not be squashed flat: water barely compresses, so it is the air spaces in your body that collapse

ideas.title: What if you held your breath for as long as you could?
ideas.setting: A swimming pool, with a cutaway of the lungs and blood
ideas.hook: What if you held your breath for as long as you could?
ideas.the surprising true point: The desperate urge to breathe comes from carbon dioxide building up, not from running out of oxygen
ideas.note: Told as checked: the urge to breathe comes mainly from carbon dioxide; the exact break point is unresolved, so no single 'alarm' is claimed.

ideas.title: Mount St. Helens, second by second
ideas.setting: The mountain and the forest around it, Washington State, 18 May 1980
ideas.hook: Mount St. Helens, second by second
ideas.the surprising true point: It did not blow its top first: the north side slid away in a giant landslide, and that uncorked a blast that shot out sideways

ideas.title: What if lightning struck your plane?
ideas.setting: A passenger jet inside a storm cloud, with a cutaway of the cabin
ideas.hook: What if lightning struck your plane?
ideas.the surprising true point: It happens to airliners regularly: the current runs through the metal skin and leaves again, so the people inside are shielded

ideas.title: What if the Moon orbited as close as the space station?
ideas.setting: A coastal city at night, with the Moon filling the sky
ideas.hook: What if the Moon orbited as close as the space station?
ideas.the surprising true point: It could not stay a moon: that close, Earth's tides would pull it apart into a ring long before you could enjoy the view

ideas.title: What if you fell into Jupiter?
ideas.setting: Above Jupiter's cloud tops, then down through the layers
ideas.hook: What if you fell into Jupiter?
ideas.the surprising true point: There is no ground to hit: you keep sinking while pressure and heat rise, as the Galileo probe showed before it went silent

ideas.title: Tacoma Narrows Bridge, minute by minute
ideas.setting: The suspension bridge over Puget Sound, Washington State, 7 November 1940
ideas.hook: The bridge that twisted itself apart, minute by minute
ideas.the surprising true point: It was not a storm and not simple resonance: a steady wind fed a twisting motion that kept growing, and no person died

ideas.title: What if the Earth had rings like Saturn?
ideas.setting: The night sky seen from the equator, from a mid-latitude city and from near the pole
ideas.hook: What if the Earth had rings like Saturn?
ideas.the surprising true point: They would look different from every place on Earth: a thin bright line overhead at the equator, a huge arch across the sky further away, and their shadow would darken the winter half of the planet

ideas.title: The Carrington Event, hour by hour
ideas.setting: An observatory near London and telegraph offices, 1 to 2 September 1859
ideas.hook: The day the Sun set telegraph offices on fire
ideas.the surprising true point: A solar storm drove currents through telegraph wires strong enough to spark and to run lines with the batteries unplugged, and auroras were seen far closer to the equator than normal

ideas.title: What if you drank only seawater?
ideas.setting: A life raft on the open ocean, with a cutaway of a kidney
ideas.hook: What if you drank only seawater?
ideas.the surprising true point: Seawater is saltier than the saltiest urine your kidneys can make, so every mouthful costs you more water than it gives

ideas.title: The Wright brothers' first flight, second by second
ideas.setting: The dunes at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, 17 December 1903
ideas.hook: The first aeroplane flight lasted 12 seconds
ideas.the surprising true point: The first powered flight covered about 37 metres, less than the wingspan of a modern jumbo jet, and the fourth flight that same day lasted almost a minute

ideas.title: What if you dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon?
ideas.setting: The lunar surface beside a lander, with an astronaut holding both
ideas.hook: What if you dropped a hammer and a feather on the Moon?
ideas.the surprising true point: They land at the same moment: with no air, everything falls at the same rate, as Apollo 15 showed on camera in 1971, and they fall about six times more slowly than on Earth

ideas.title: What if you flew at 99% of the speed of light for one year?
ideas.setting: A small starship leaving Earth, with two clocks side by side: one on board, one at home
ideas.hook: What if you flew at 99% of the speed of light for one year?
ideas.the surprising true point: Your clock really runs slower: one year on board is about seven years on Earth, so you come home younger than the people you left

ideas.title: What if you stood on the surface of Venus?
ideas.setting: The rocky plain of Venus under thick orange cloud, with an old lander nearby
ideas.hook: What if you stood on the surface of Venus?
ideas.the surprising true point: The air is so dense it presses like the sea almost a kilometre down, and it is hot enough to melt lead: the toughest landers lasted only about two hours

ideas.title: The Great Molasses Flood, minute by minute
ideas.setting: A giant storage tank beside the harbour, Boston North End, 15 January 1919
ideas.hook: The day a wave of molasses flooded Boston
ideas.the surprising true point: Molasses is not always slow: when the tank burst, a wave several metres high moved faster than a person can run, and the cold then made it set around everything it reached

ideas.title: What if you made tea on top of Mount Everest?
ideas.setting: A camp stove on the summit ridge, with a cutaway of the water and the thin air above it
ideas.hook: What if you made tea on top of Mount Everest?
ideas.the surprising true point: Water boils at only about 70 degrees there, because the air pressure is about a third of sea level: boiling tells you about pressure, not just heat

ideas.title: What if everyone on Earth jumped at the same time?
ideas.setting: A packed stadium, then the whole planet seen from space with every person gathered in one place
ideas.hook: What if everyone on Earth jumped at the same time?
ideas.the surprising true point: The planet would not notice: Earth is so much heavier than all of us together that it moves by far less than the width of an atom, and it moves straight back when we land

ideas.title: The Vasa, minute by minute
ideas.setting: Stockholm harbour, 10 August 1628: a brand-new warship setting sail in front of the city
ideas.hook: The warship that sank on its first voyage, minute by minute
ideas.the surprising true point: It sailed barely more than a kilometre: the ship was too tall and too narrow for its weight, a gust of wind leaned it over, and water poured in through the open gun ports

ideas.title: What if raindrops fell with no air to slow them down?
ideas.setting: A rainy city street with umbrellas, and a cutaway of one drop falling from the cloud
ideas.hook: What if raindrops fell with no air to slow them down?
ideas.the surprising true point: Air is what makes rain gentle: a real raindrop lands at only a few metres a second, but from a cloud two kilometres up with no air it would arrive at about 700 km/h

ideas.title: What if you opened a plane door mid-flight?
ideas.setting: The cabin of an airliner at cruising height, with a cutaway of the door and the thin air outside
ideas.hook: What if you opened a plane door mid-flight?
ideas.the surprising true point: You could not: the door is a plug that opens inward first, and the cabin air presses on it with a force of several tonnes, far more than any person can pull

ideas.title: What if you tried to swim in a pool of mercury?
ideas.setting: A laboratory tank of liquid mercury beside an ordinary swimming pool, with you stepping into each
ideas.hook: What if you tried to swim in a pool of mercury?
ideas.the surprising true point: You could not sink: mercury is about thirteen times denser than water, so you would float on top with most of your body above the surface (and its vapour is poisonous, so nobody should try)

ideas.title: What if you shouted in space?
ideas.setting: Two astronauts outside a space station, a few metres apart, with the sound drawn as waves
ideas.hook: What if you shouted in space?
ideas.the surprising true point: Nobody would hear you, even a metre away: sound is a wave in matter and there is almost none out there, but touch your helmets together and your voice travels through the glass

ideas.title: Lituya Bay, second by second
ideas.setting: A narrow Alaskan fjord ringed by forested mountains, with a fishing boat at anchor, 9 July 1958
ideas.hook: The tallest wave ever recorded, second by second
ideas.the surprising true point: It was not an ocean tsunami: an earthquake dropped a mountainside into the head of a narrow bay, and the splash stripped trees from the opposite slope to about half a kilometre above the water, yet people on a boat in the bay rode it out and lived

ideas.title: What if all the gold ever mined were melted into one cube?
ideas.setting: A city square with a tennis court and office buildings for scale, then the Earth cut away to show where the rest of the gold is
ideas.hook: What if all the gold ever mined were melted into one cube?
ideas.the surprising true point: It would be far smaller than people expect: a single cube only about as wide as a tennis court is long, because gold is so dense, and most of the planet's gold sank to the core long ago
